title: Correlation Breadcrumbs & Span Zoom — request drilldown composer
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design a lightweight ‘Correlation Breadcrumbs’ composer that sits above the request timeline and lets engineers quickly trace a user request across services. The composer should: 1) display the active correlation IDs (request ID, trace ID, session ID) as a compact, editable breadcrumb trail; 2) allow quick scope changes (trace-only / request-only / session) and toggle span-level detail; 3) provide a smooth zoom and scrub interaction on the span timeline with hover previews that reveal span metadata without a full panel load; 4) support keyboard-first filtering and copy-to-clipboard for correlation IDs; 5) paginate/stream spans to avoid blocking the console for large traces. Focus on discoverability for first-time users while keeping the canvas dense for power users.
acceptance_criteria: Breadcrumb composer is visible at top of timeline and shows up to 3 active correlation keys with clear labels
User can click a breadcrumb to filter all timeline rows to that correlation ID within 1s latency
Timeline supports 3 zoom levels (overview, mid, detail) with scrub preview showing span name, duration, and service
Hovering a condensed span opens a micro-preview; clicking opens the full span panel in the right rail
Prototype linked in mockups has keyboard navigation (Tab/Arrow) and copy button for IDs
Design includes states for empty traces, truncated IDs, and long-running spans with pagination hints
decisions: Use a compact breadcrumb chip pattern instead of full filter chips to reduce vertical noise
Default to showing Request ID + Trace ID; Session ID collapsed under a dropdown for most traces
Micro-previews will be client-side rendered with lazy-loaded metadata to avoid blocking render
Zoom levels will be anchored to the timeline’s time extent rather than fixed pixel widths
Copy-to-clipboard exposed on hover to reduce primary clicks and support quick correlation sharing
open_questions: Should correlation breadcrumbs persist when navigating between different requests in the same session?
Do we expose all correlation key types (user_id, session_id, request_id) or only the canonical three?
Performance budget: what is the maximum allowed latency for applying a breadcrumb filter on large traces?
Accessibility: confirm ARIA patterns for timeline scrubbing with engineering
